tutorial.title: State with useState
tutorial.seoTitle: React useState Tutorial: Managing Component State

chapters.description: Why the value does not change immediately, and what batching means for your code.

chapters.title: State in Practice

questions.question: Why can a plain local variable not hold values that change over time?
options: Variables are read only inside components
Changing it does not trigger a re-render, and it is reinitialised on the next render
React forbids let inside components
Variables cannot hold numbers in JSX
questions.explanation: A local variable is recreated on every render and changing it tells React nothing. State solves both problems: React remembers the value and re-renders when it changes.

questions.question: What does count log here after one click?
options: undefined
It throws an error
questions.explanation: Setters schedule an update; they do not change the current render's variable. `count` is still 0 in this handler and becomes 1 on the next render.

questions.question: Starting from 0, what is count after this handler runs?
questions.explanation: All three calls read the same `count` from the current render, so each schedules 'set it to 1'. Use the updater form, `setCount(c => c + 1)`, to get 3.

questions.question: When should you use the updater form of a setter?
options: Whenever the new value is computed from the previous one
Only inside effects
Only when the state is an object
Never, it is deprecated
questions.explanation: The updater receives the latest pending value, so updates that build on the previous one stack correctly and cannot read a stale value.

questions.question: Why does this fail to update the screen?
options: push is not a function on state arrays
The array is mutated so its reference is unchanged, and React sees no new state
setTags must be called twice
Arrays cannot be stored in state
questions.explanation: React compares by reference. `push` mutates the same array, so the reference matches the previous state and the update is skipped. Pass a new array instead.

questions.question: Which of these should NOT be stored in state?
options: The list of items a user has added
A total that can be calculated from the list of items
The current value of a text input
Whether a dialog is open
questions.explanation: Anything derivable should be computed during render. Storing it duplicates the source of truth and lets the two drift apart.

questions.question: Two sibling components need the same value. What should you do?
options: Duplicate the state in both components
Lift the state to their closest common parent and pass it down
Store it in a module level variable
Pass state upward through a prop
questions.explanation: Lifting state up puts one source of truth in the closest common parent, which then passes the value and an updater down to both children.

questions.question: Update an item without mutating the array
questions.explanation: Returning a new array is what lets React notice the change.

editor.title: Mark an item as done
editor.instructions: Complete markDone so it returns a NEW array where the item with the given id has done set to true. Do not modify the original array.

tests.name: The matching item is marked done
The original array is not mutated
tests.code: var list = [{id:1,done:false}]; markDone(list, 1); return list[0].done === false;
